subject: GTM consent-signal interoperability and telemetry export questions
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: product-privacy@acme-retail.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GTM consent signals + telemetry export — questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We like the idea of routing telemetry through Redwood Console so our data team can analyze model usage but we have a few privacy and data-flow questions before sign-off from our privacy team. High-level: we need to understand what signals are sent from our website to Redwood when we use Google Tag Manager (GTM) + Consent Mode.

Specific asks:
- Does Redwood rely on any browser cookies set by our site when collecting telemetry from the Console SDK, or do you capture only the consent signals from GTM?
- If we enable Consent Mode v2, can we pass the consent_state to Redwood so events are marked as non-personal when consent is denied?
- What PII (if any) is included in telemetry exports that Redwood stores in your analytics pipeline?
- Can we get a minimal dataflow diagram showing telemetry ingestion, intermediate storage, and any subprocessors that will see the telemetry?

Our privacy team is particularly concerned about transfers outside the EU. Can we scope the answers to EU visitors first?

Attaching a draft of our DPA redlines that the legal team asked me to share.

[Attachment: acme-dpa-redlines.pdf (pdf, 28KB)]

Appreciate a quick note on whether a short call with your legal/security folks would help.

Best,
Emma
Product & Privacy Liaison
Acme Retail

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GTM consent signals + telemetry export — questions

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura from Legal and Stephanie from Customer Success so we can cover legal, telemetry, and implementation.

Quick answers up front so you have something to share with privacy while we prepare a short dataflow:
- Redwood Console SDK does not set marketing cookies by default. Telemetry events sent via the SDK include page and event metadata (path, referrer, event_name) and a request-level context. We do not collect browser-stored cookies unless you explicitly configure the SDK to forward them.
- We support Consent Mode v2 signals. If your GTM tags push consent_state to the dataLayer, Redwood can accept that field and store it as a consent flag on the event, which you can then filter out of analytics exports.
- By default telemetry does not include user identifiers. However, if you configure identity forwarding (recommended for session correlation), that will include a customer-supplied user_id. We can disable identity forwarding for EU-only traffic.

Laura/Steph — can one of you take the privacy/technical details (and attach the short dataflow diagram) so Emma's team has a record for their privacy review?

Next step: propose a 30-min call Mon/Tue next week — I'm flexible.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GTM consent signals + telemetry export — questions

Hi Emma,

Thanks for sharing the redlines. A few legal points specifically related to telemetry and transfers:
1) Data classification: from a DPA perspective we consider "telemetry" to be operational usage metadata. It may contain customer-supplied identifiers if you enable them — that will be reflected in the dataflow.
2) Transfers: Redwood offers EU-hosted telemetry storage for EU visitors (we can pin telemetry events to our EU region and avoid transfers to the US). If you require contractual guarantees, we can add a data localization addendum to the DPA.
3) Subprocessors: our telemetry pipeline uses two subprocessors for short-term buffering and analytics (a managed Kafka cluster provider and a cloud storage provider). We will supply the subprocessor names and SCCs/additional safeguards on request.

Two asks from my side:
- Please confirm whether Acme will forward any email or service-identifiers (email hash, crm_id) in the telemetry project. If yes, we need to mark that in the DPA and discuss pseudonymization options.
- If you need EU-only processing, confirm which models (Console export, raw event dumps) need to be localized.

I attached a short excerpt from our DPA that shows the telemetry clause and subprocessor notification flow.

[Attachment: redwood-dpa-excerpt.pdf (pdf, 34KB)]

Happy to join a call with the privacy team; Rishi, please coordinate times.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: product-privacy@acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GTM consent signals + telemetry export — questions

Laura — thanks, that helps. Quick clarifications from our end:
- We will NOT forward email addresses or raw PII in telemetry. We do consider a CRM id (crm_id) as a pseudonymized identifier; we can choose to stop forwarding that for EU visitors only.
- EU-only processing: we would like Console export (aggregated analytics and per-route latency metrics) to remain in EU. Raw event dumps can be US for now.

I've uploaded the GTM dataLayer example and our current consent implementation (Consent Mode v2 + CMP integration) — attaching here. Please take a look when you have a moment.

[Attachment: acme-gtm-datalayer-example.json (json, 6KB)]

Also: can you share a minimal PNG of your telemetry ingestion flow that we can attach to our privacy memo?

Thanks,
Emma

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GTM consent signals + telemetry export — questions

Emma — hi, Tessa from Security here. Quick technical notes and confirmations for Acme's privacy memo:
- We'll provide a minimal telemetry dataflow PNG (no credentials, only system names and regions) showing where events land and which subprocessors see the data. Expect that in the next email.
- For Consent Mode v2, Redwood ingests the consent_state field but only stores it as an attribute on the event. You can configure retention rules so events marked as "denied" are either not written to long-term analytics storage or are purged after a short buffer window.
- Subprocessor details: managed Kafka (BufferCo) is used for <48h buffering; our EU storage is on EU-region ObjectStore (we will provide vendor names & SCCs in the subprocessor list).

Action items:
1) Rishi to schedule a 30-min call for Tue 23 Jun or Wed 24 Jun.
2) Tessa will send the PNG and subprocessor list as a separate email and include SCC references.
3) Laura will prepare the DPA data-localization addendum draft for Acme's review.

If that works, we can mark this thread as covered for the privacy review and move to contract redlines.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
